question: After the release-ordering bug is fixed and the branch is refreshed, should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout?
rationale: The consent gate is the right Android layer, but disabling existing opt-ins and changing Play release automation are upgrade and release-policy choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Fix ordering and accept rollout
options.body: Require the release-ref ordering fix, refresh the branch, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, and land the consent rollout.

options.title: Revise disclosure or release lane first
options.body: Request different disclosure wording, consent-version behavior, or Data Safety upload semantics before accepting the rollout.

options.title: Hold until Play materials are ready
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until external Play Console, privacy-policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship with the code.

recommendation.title: Fix ordering and accept rollout
recommendation.body: Require the release-ref ordering fix, refresh the branch, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, and land the consent rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Android settings and release-lane work makes this the best available owner for the rollout and release-ordering decision.
